IT professional liability concerns allegations that a company's professional service caused a client loss. It differs from insuring laptops and from restoring the company's own systems after an attack. A Moldova software firm should start with its actual services and contracts. A general professional-liability product description does not confirm acceptance of every IT activity, client country or contractual promise.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. The 2027 scenarios are planning examples, not forecasts or confirmation of individual insurance terms.

Who should review the requirement?

Software developers, system integrators, IT consultants and managed-service providers should compare client requirements with the services delivered. Describe development, implementation, support and data migration separately. Identify subcontractors and who approves their work. A broad business classification or a website portfolio cannot replace the current activity description submitted for assessment.

For the wider professional-indemnity question before considering IT-specific services, read Professional indemnity insurance in Moldova: services, claims and limits. This general article does not confirm acceptance of your technology activity or international client terms.

Which losses need separate answers?

A programming defect, faulty configuration and failed migration can generate different demands. Separate correcting the company's own work from consequential loss alleged by the client. Ask how investigation and defence expenses are treated and whether they share the main limit. These questions do not establish that a particular cost is insured. Keep acceptance records, change requests and test results linked to the delivered version.

Important wording and exclusions

Review contractual penalties, promises exceeding the ordinary scope of the service, intellectual-property allegations, cyber events and known complaints separately. Check the applicable dates, including any retroactive date and claims-notification conditions. A retroactive date is a contractual boundary whose effect must be read with the whole wording. Buying a policy after a complaint does not automatically protect the known circumstance.

INTACT's public page describes general professional liability. INTACT: professional liability presentation. Checked 25 November 2026. It does not establish acceptance of IT activities, client countries or AI-assisted services. No IT-specific rate or policy wording has been obtained.

What determines the price?

Activities, revenue, client sectors and countries, requested limits, deductible, loss history and contract wording may affect assessment. There is no verified IT-specific 2027 premium in this article. A broad public tariff for another professional-liability category cannot responsibly be used as a quotation for a software business. Compare offers using the same facts and identify any unresolved acceptance conditions.

Planning for AI-assisted work in 2027

If the company adds generative-AI coding, a new subcontractor or automated production deployment, review testing, approval and client commitments before renewal. These are business-planning scenarios, not predictions of new Moldova insurance obligations. In an illustrative project, a generated code change passes a basic test but alters an invoicing rule. Preserve the requirement, review and release evidence rather than assuming the AI supplier or insurer automatically assumes responsibility.

Documents for assessment

Prepare service descriptions, revenue breakdowns requested by the insurer, anonymized contract clauses, client countries, subcontracting arrangements and a factual complaint history. Do not send source code, credentials or customer data through public forms. Insurance ING Broker SRL acts as broker; acceptance and claims decisions belong to the insurer under the contract.

A 2026 AI-related signal, not proof of PI coverage

ENISA's 22 September 2026 release discusses AI-related cyber exposure alongside its 2025 EU evidence.

This neither establishes Moldova professional-liability demand nor proves that a PI policy accepts AI-assisted services. Our editorial 2027 planning recommendation is to update the declared service description when AI integration changes what a client receives. Record where human review occurs, who approves release and how testing matches the client's actual use. Discuss the resulting professional-service question separately from cybersecurity and own-system restoration. Such preparation can reveal which contracts need assessment, without predicting claims or treating a European technical observation as an insurance endorsement, legal requirement or promise of compensation.

Practical risk prevention

Use agreed requirements, change approval, peer review and traceable testing before releasing work. Separate test data from customers' production information. Document acceptance and unresolved defects, and review subcontracted output. For AI-assisted changes, retain the human review and testing evidence rather than treating generated code as verified. These controls support risk reduction without guaranteeing an error-free service or an insurer's acceptance.

Three IT losses: correction, client demand and own incident

These are hypothetical decision situations, not actual client cases or a list of accepted benefits.

  • The firm must correct its own code: keep the agreed requirement, defect and correction records. Rectifying the deliverable is not automatically identical to a client's claim for a separate loss.
  • A client alleges that a released change interrupted its operations: preserve version, approval, tests and acceptance. A technical cause, legal responsibility and insurance treatment are different findings, even when the client gives one total amount.
  • The firm's own data becomes inaccessible: distinguish restoration and internal interruption from a professional-service allegation. Compare the relevant cyber question rather than assuming the PI label accepts every digital consequence.

Frequently asked questions

What determines the price of an IT professional-liability enquiry?

Describe services, revenue, client industries and countries, contract wording, subcontracting and complaint history. State the requested limit and deductible. Compare identical facts; a generic rate for another profession cannot responsibly be presented as an IT quotation.

Which documents should a software company prepare?

Useful materials include service descriptions, anonymized contract clauses, acceptance and change processes, client countries and a factual complaint history. Provide only necessary records through an agreed channel. Do not attach credentials, customer data or source code to a public request.

What should be preserved after a client alleges an error?

Keep the demand, requirements, relevant versions, testing and acceptance evidence with dates. Seek appropriate legal and technical help and follow the applicable policy procedure. An allegation, established responsibility and an insurer's acceptance are different matters.

How should PI and cyber be compared for the same incident?

Separate harm alleged by the client from the firm's own response, system restoration and interruption costs. Ask which actual wording addresses each consequence. Neither product label confirms that all parts are accepted, and overlapping descriptions do not prove duplicate protection.

For the firm's own incident response and digital interruption questions, compare Cyber insurance for SMEs: risks, preparation and policy questions. A client demand and internal restoration costs are not automatically the same accepted loss category.

How do retroactive and notification provisions affect the comparison?

Ask the insurer to explain the dates and conditions together using the actual service and complaint timeline. Do not assume an earlier project or a known complaint is accepted by a new policy. Preserve the written explanation with the wording reviewed.
